ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are two concentric circles, and the annular region between the outer circle and the inner circle is colored gray. On the right side there is a vertical line segment AB, with the upper end labeled B and the lower end labeled A. A and B are on the outer circle, so AB is a chord of the outer circle; this chord is tangent to the small circle on the right side of the inner circle. The problem gives AB = 16. Then reason: Let the radius of the outer circle be R, and the radius of the inner circle be r. Because AB is tangent to the inner circle, the perpendicular distance from the common center to chord AB is r. The chord length is 16, therefore the half-chord length is 8. Connect the center of the circles to an endpoint of the chord, and a right triangle can be obtained, whose hypotenuse is R and whose two legs are r and 8, so R^2 = r^2 + 8^2. Therefore R^2 - r^2 = 64. The area of the gray annular region is π(R^2 - r^2) = 64π.

method.method_draft: Read the image as two concentric circles with the grey region being the annulus between them. The vertical segment AB is a chord of the outer circle and is tangent to the inner circle at its rightmost point, so the perpendicular distance from the common center to chord AB equals the inner radius r. From the text, AB = 16, so half the chord is 8. Let R be the outer radius. Using the right triangle formed by the outer radius to an endpoint of the chord, the center-to-chord distance r, and half-chord 8, get R^2 = r^2 + 8^2, hence R^2 - r^2 = 64. The grey area is the difference of circle areas, pi(R^2 - r^2), so it equals 64 pi.
